thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Edge Lower After Weak Jobs Data, Rising Trade Tensions

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Edge Lower After Weak Jobs Data, Rising Trade Tensions
text:
By Anora M. Gaudiano and Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
U.S. economy adds 103,000 jobs in March
U.S. stocks traded lower on Friday as investors digested a weaker-than-expected jobs report and grappled with continued trade war fears following President Donald Trump's proposal of fresh tariffs against China.
Trump announced late Thursday that he was considering tariffs on another $100 billion in Chinese goods, which would triple the amount of imports facing levies.
What are main benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 205 points, or 0.8%, to 24,298. The S&P 500 index dropped 16 points, or 0.6%, to 2,645. Meanwhile the Nasdaq Composite Index declined 43 points, or 0.6%, to 7,031.
Equities fell hard earlier this week, then proceeded to recover, but Friday's session is promising volatility to which investors are becoming accustomed. With one more session to go, Dow is looking at a gain of 1% for the week, while the S&P 500 is poised to put on 0.2%. The Nasdaq Composite is looking for a weekly loss of 0.2%.
The major U.S. stock indexes posted their first three-day gain in a month (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-set-up-for-more-gains-as-trade-fears-stay-muted-2018-04-05) on Thursday.
Read:Dimon: Investors underestimate threat of 'drastic action' by Fed, other central banks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jpmorgans-dimon-investors-beware-drastic-action-by-fed-other-central-banks-2018-04-05)
What's driving markets
Futures markets were already pointing to a lower open even before the disappointing jobs report. The U.S. economy added just 103,000 new jobs in March (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-103000-jobs-in-march-in-smallest-gain-since-last-fall-2018-04-06)to mark the smallest increase since last fall and well below the 170,000 forecast by economists polled by MarketWatch. But the latest report on employment still shows the tightest labor market in nearly two decades.
Rather, investors appeared to be focused on a trade battle between the two largest economies.
The White House said in a statement (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-statement-requesting-100-billion-in-additional-china-tariffs-2018-04-05) after the market close Thursday that Trump has asked the U.S. Trade Representative to consider an extra $100 billion in Chinese goods to face tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/futures-fall-as-trump-seeks-100-billion-in-additional-china-tariffs-2018-04-05) and to identify the products that could be targeted.
Read:Republican senator on Trump's latest tariff threat: 'This is nuts' (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/republican-senator-on-trumps-latest-tariff-threat-this-is-nuts-2018-04-05)
U.S. stock futures immediately tumbled on Thursday's news, action which continued into Friday's session, though losses weren't as severe as in reactions to other, recent trade rumblings. China's commerce department responded to the latest tariff threat by saying it will respond with countermeasures if needed.
"The Chinese side will follow suit to the end, not hesitate to pay any price, resolutely counterattack and take new comprehensive measures in response," said a ministry statement via its website (http://www.mofcom.gov.cn/article/ae/ag/201804/20180402728771.shtml), citing an unnamed spokesman. The statement added that China "doesn't want" a trade war, but is not afraid to fight one."
"If this trade war comes to pass, it will be an evenly matched total war between China and the U.S. economies, and not some small scuffle. It would be delusional for the U.S. to think it will be victorious at the end of this trade war," China's state-run Global Times said in an editorial (http://www.globaltimes.cn/content/1096648.shtml).
Away from trade, Fed Chairman Jerome Powell is set to speak to the Economic Club of Chicago at 1:30 p.m. Eastern. Later, San Francisco Fed President John Williams is scheduled to give a speech in Santa Rosa, Calif., at 4 p.m.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
What are strategists saying?
"Part of the problem why we may see weak jobs growth is because it is hard to find qualified workers and not because the economy is slowing. The job market is really tight," said Maris Ogg, president at Tower Bridge Advisors.
Ogg noted that markets would be right to shrug off Trump's tariff rhetoric.
"It's all a show, to prove that he is keeping his campaign promises. If he were serious about tariffs, why did he hire Larry Kudlow, who is well-known "free-trade" economist," Ogg said.
Opinion:Stock guru who called S&P 500 gains sees no new market high before October (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-guru-who-called-sp-500-gains-sees-no-new-market-high-before-october-2018-04-06)
What stocks are moving?
Salesforce.com Inc.(CRM) shares were down 1% after the cloud-computing company confirmed late Thursday it will issue $2.5 billion in bonds to help finance its purchase
Shares of Micron Technology Inc.'s stock(MU) slid 3.6% a day after UBS initiated coverage of the semiconductor group with a sell rating. And those analyst said the semiconductor industry will face headwinds this year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-nvidia-weigh-as-chip-makers-hamper-tech-gains-2018-04-05).
In the same sector, Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) was down nearly 1%. Short seller Citron Research on Thursday tweeted that it sees shares falling below $200 soon.
Target Corp.(TGT)agreed to pay more than $3.7 million (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/target-to-pay-37-million-to-settle-suit-over-racial-bias-in-job-screening-2018-04-05) to settle a lawsuit over racial bias in screening job applicants. The retailer also said it would overhaul its job-screening guidelines.
Apple Inc.(AAPL) shares slipped 0.8%. Court documents revealed Thursday that Chief Executive Tim Cook will be deposed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-ceo-tim-cook-to-be-deposed-in-qualcomm-lawsuit-2018-04-05) on June 27 in chip maker Qualcomm Inc.'s(QCOM) lawsuit against the iPhone maker.
What are other markets doing?
Asian stocks had a mixed day (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-waver-after-trumps-latest-broadside-against-china-2018-04-05), with the Hong Kong Hang Seng Index rising 1% on bets that the latest Trump tariff threat may not develop into any real issue.
After logging strong advances on Thursday, European stocks fell across the board (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-markets-tip-lower-as-trade-worries-resurface-to-rattle-investors-2018-04-06). Gold futures eased modestly, while the ICE U.S. Dollar Index was flat. A pullback for perceived riskier assets took a toll on oil prices , which fell 0.4%.
